## Challenge

Make a fused 12 V lamp operate through a verified automotive relay. Explain terminals 30, 85, 86, 87, and 87a, then diagnose a reversible fault from voltage evidence.

## Safety boundary

- Verify the exact case diagram and datasheet.
- Use a relay socket and lamp as the normal load.
- Power off before moving wires or using continuity mode.
- Never connect the coil, lamp, or horn directly to BeagleBone GPIO.
- A real horn is a short teacher-supervised extension only.

## Pathways

| Minimum | Proficient | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Identify the relay; map the socket; operate a fused NO lamp; measure source, coil, and lamp voltage. | Add KVL/KCL labels, all voltage test points, released/energized tables, and diagnose two faults. | Use a transistor/MOSFET driver, flyback protection, default-off Python control, and separate fused load supply. |

## Parts to request

Verified 12 V relay and socket, fused/current-limited 12 V source, fuse holder, rated lamp, switch, insulated leads, multimeter, and—only for the extension—approved driver parts.

## Gates

1. Datasheet and socket map approved.
2. Power-off continuity states approved.
3. Fused lamp build approved.
4. Voltage table and two fault diagnoses complete.
5. Driver schematic approved before any BeagleBone connection.

## Submit

Approved schematic, terminal/datasheet record, calculations, predicted/measured voltage table, KVL/KCL checks, fault log, one clear photograph, safety decisions, and reflection.
